classification.difficultyReason: Rearranges standard sphere rate equations, interprets decreasing rates and reuses the radius rate from part (b).

content.prompt: Gas escapes a spherical bubble so that the bubble always remains a sphere.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the rate of decrease of the radius when the radius is 5 mm if the volume of the sphere is decreasing at a constant rate of $75\text{ mm}^3$ per sec.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}V&=\frac43\pi r^3\\\frac{dV}{dr}&=4\pi r^2\\\frac{dV}{dt}&=-75\text{ mm}^3\!/\text{s}\\\frac{dr}{dt}&=\frac{dr}{dV}\frac{dV}{dt}\\\frac{dr}{dt}&=\frac{1}{4\pi r^2}(-75)\end{aligned}$$
When $r=5\text{ mm}$,
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dr}{dt}&=-\frac{75}{4\pi(25)}\\\frac{dr}{dt}&=-\frac{3}{4\pi}\text{ mm/s}.\end{aligned}$$
The radius decreases at $\dfrac{3}{4\pi}\text{ mm/s}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the rate of decrease of the radius when the radius is 12 mm if the surface area of the sphere is decreasing at $24\text{ mm}^2$ per sec.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}S&=4\pi r^2\\\frac{dS}{dr}&=8\pi r\\\frac{dS}{dt}&=-24\text{ mm}^2\!/\text{s}\\\frac{dr}{dt}&=\frac{dr}{dS}\frac{dS}{dt}\\\frac{dr}{dt}&=\frac{1}{8\pi r}(-24)\end{aligned}$$
When $r=12\text{ mm}$,
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dr}{dt}&=-\frac{24}{96\pi}\\\frac{dr}{dt}&=-\frac{1}{4\pi}\text{ mm/s}.\end{aligned}$$
The radius decreases at $\dfrac{1}{4\pi}\text{ mm/s}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the rate of decrease of the volume when the radius is 12 mm if the surface area of the sphere is decreasing at $24\text{ mm}^2$ per sec.

answer.worked:
From part (b), $\dfrac{dr}{dt}=-\dfrac{1}{4\pi}\text{ mm/s}$ when $r=12\text{ mm}$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dV}{dt}&=\frac{dV}{dr}\frac{dr}{dt}\\\frac{dV}{dt}&=4\pi r^2\frac{dr}{dt}\\\frac{dV}{dt}&=4\pi(144)\left(-\frac{1}{4\pi}\right)\\\frac{dV}{dt}&=-144\text{ mm}^3\!/\text{s}.\end{aligned}$$
The volume decreases at $144\text{ mm}^3\!/\text{s}$.
